en: softly and fluffily; in soft, rounded clumps

examples.ko: 따뜻한 우유 위에 거품이 몽글몽글 올라왔어요.
examples.en: Soft, small bubbles puffed up on top of the warm milk.
Soft, round clouds are floating in the sky.
The soft tofu is bubbling away in soft curds.
A soft excitement is blooming in my heart.

examples.ko: 비누 거품이 몽글몽글 생겨서 아이가 좋아해요.
examples.en: Soft soap bubbles are forming, and the child loves it.
I watched the puffs of smoke rising for a long time.

explain: 작고 부드러운 덩어리가 동글동글 모이거나 피어오르는 모습에 써요. 거품, 구름, 연기처럼 눈에 보이는 것뿐 아니라 '마음이 몽글몽글하다'처럼 따뜻하고 간질간질한 감정에도 써요.

phrases.en: Hearing that makes my heart feel warm and fuzzy.
phrases.nuance_ko: '몽글몽글'에 '-하다'를 붙여 상태나 감정을 말해요. 마음이 따뜻하고 간질간질할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding -하다 turns it into a state or feeling, often a warm, tingly one in the heart.

phrases.en: Steam rose softly in little puffs from the hot tea.
phrases.nuance_ko: 연기나 김, 거품이 작게 뭉쳐서 올라오는 모습에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for smoke, steam or bubbles rising in small soft puffs.
phrases.en_equiv: to rise in soft little puffs

phrases.en: The sky is full of soft, puffy clouds.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뒤에 오는 명사를 꾸며 줄 때는 '몽글몽글한'으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use 몽글몽글한 to describe a noun that follows.

explain_en: It describes small, soft clumps gathering or rising in a round shape, such as bubbles, clouds and smoke. It is also used for warm, fluttery feelings, as in '마음이 몽글몽글하다'.

examples.en: The fallen leaves rustle in the wind.
The plastic bag keeps rustling and it bothers me.

examples.ko: 밤새 쥐가 바스락거리는 소리에 잠을 못 잤어요.
examples.en: I couldn't sleep because of a mouse rustling all night.

examples.ko: 마른 풀을 밟으면 바스락거리는 소리가 나요.
examples.en: When you step on dry grass, it makes a rustling sound.
The child played rustling around under the blanket.

examples.ko: 종이가 바스락거리지 않게 조심히 넘겨 주세요.
examples.en: Please turn the pages carefully so the paper doesn't rustle.

explain: '바스락' 소리가 계속 나거나 반복될 때 써요. '바스락'이 한 번 나는 소리라면 '바스락거리다'는 이어지는 소리예요. 밤에 방해되는 소리나 조용한 곳에서 들리는 작은 소리에 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: I like the sound of leaves rustling.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-는'을 붙여 뒤의 명사를 꾸밀 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: With '-는' it modifies the noun that follows.

phrases.en: This plastic doesn't rustle, so it's quiet.
phrases.nuance_ko: 소리가 나지 않는다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say something does not make that rustling sound.

phrases.en: The person next to me keeps rustling.
phrases.nuance_ko: '바스락거리다'보다 더 크고 둔한 소리예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A louder, duller sound than 바스락거리다.

explain_en: Light, dry rustle sound, small or thin things (밤에 비닐봉지가 바스락거려서 잠이 깼어요.) Use it when the '바스락' sound continues or repeats. '바스락' is a single sound, while '바스락거리다' is an ongoing one. It often appears for small noises heard in a quiet place or at night.

t90.ax: The fallen leaves rustle in the wind.

examples.ko: 달리기를 했더니 이마에 땀이 송알송알 맺혔어요.
examples.en: After running, beads of sweat formed on my forehead.

examples.ko: 아침에 풀잎마다 이슬이 송알송알 맺혀 있어요.
examples.en: In the morning, dew has formed in tiny drops on every blade of grass.

examples.ko: 차가운 컵 겉에 물방울이 송알송알 생겼어요.
examples.en: Little water droplets formed on the outside of the cold cup.

examples.ko: 아이 코끝에 땀방울이 송알송알 맺힌 걸 봤어요.
examples.en: I saw tiny beads of sweat on the child's nose tip.

examples.ko: 창문에 송알송알 맺힌 빗방울이 참 예뻐요.
examples.en: The raindrops dotting the window are so pretty.

examples.ko: 뜨거운 국을 먹었더니 코에 땀이 송알송알 나요.
examples.en: After eating the hot soup, sweat is beading on my nose.

explain: 땀, 이슬, 물방울 같은 작은 방울이 여기저기 맺힌 모습에 써요. 거의 '맺히다'와 같이 나오니 '땀이 송알송알 맺히다'를 한 덩어리로 외우세요. 땀에는 '송골송골'도 자주 써요.

phrases.en: Droplets beaded on the cold cup.
phrases.nuance_ko: '송알송알'과 거의 항상 함께 나오는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Almost always paired with 'songalsongal'.

phrases.en: The beaded dew sparkles in the sunlight.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뒤에 명사를 붙여 풍경을 그릴 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used before a noun to paint a scene.

phrases.en: Sweat beaded on my nose.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뜻이 거의 같고 땀에 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Almost the same meaning, used a bit more often for sweat.

explain_en: It describes small drops such as sweat, dew or water beads forming in many places. It almost always appears with '맺히다', so learn '땀이 송알송알 맺히다' as one chunk. For sweat, '송골송골' is also commonly used.

examples.en: My mother's face keeps flickering before my eyes.
A shadow flickered outside the window and it startled me.
The moonlight is shimmering on the water.
I was sleepy and the letters in the book swam before my eyes.

examples.ko: 커튼 뒤에서 누가 어른거리는 것 같아요.
examples.en: It looks like someone is moving faintly behind the curtain.

examples.ko: 밤새 아이 모습이 눈에 어른거려서 잠을 못 잤어요.
examples.en: The child's image kept haunting me all night, so I couldn't sleep.

explain: 희미하게 보였다 안 보였다 하거나, 보고 싶은 사람의 모습이 자꾸 떠오를 때 써요. '아른거리다'와 비슷한 말이고, '눈앞에', '눈에'와 같이 자주 써요.

phrases.en: My friend's face keeps flickering before my eyes.
phrases.nuance_ko: 보고 싶은 사람이나 장면이 자꾸 떠오를 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing when a person or scene you miss keeps coming to mind.

phrases.en: I saw a shadow flickering behind the curtain.
phrases.nuance_ko: 희미하게 보였다 안 보였다 하는 것을 꾸밀 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to describe something seen faintly and intermittently.

phrases.en: Scenes of my hometown keep floating before my eyes.
phrases.nuance_ko: '어른거리다'와 비슷한 말이고, 조금 더 작고 가벼운 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A similar word to 어른거리다 with a slightly smaller, lighter feel.

explain_en: It is used when something appears and disappears faintly, or when the image of someone you miss keeps coming to mind. '아른거리다' is a similar word, and it is often used with '눈앞에' or '눈에'.

t90.ax: The moonlight is shimmering on the water.

examples.ko: 물살이 빠른 여울에서 아이들이 물놀이를 했어요.
examples.en: The children played in the water at the fast-flowing shallows.

examples.ko: 이 여울은 물이 얕아서 걸어서 건널 수 있어요.
examples.en: The water in this shallow stretch of rapids is low, so you can cross it on foot.

examples.ko: 여울 소리가 시원해서 한참 앉아 있었어요.
examples.en: The sound of the rapids was so refreshing that I sat there for a while.

examples.ko: 낚시꾼들이 여울을 따라 천천히 걸어 올라갔어요.
examples.en: The anglers slowly walked upstream along the rapids.

examples.ko: 강이 좁아지는 곳에 작은 여울이 생겼어요.
examples.en: A small stretch of rapids formed where the river narrows.
The fish are gathered below the rapids.

explain: 강바닥이 얕거나 좁아서 물살이 빠르고 소리가 나는 곳이에요. 글이나 노래에서 풍경을 그릴 때 어울리는 말이에요. 좁아져서 물이 세게 흐르는 곳은 '여울목'이라고도 해요.

phrases.en: You can hear the water loudly at the narrow rapids.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물이 좁아져서 세게 흐르는 곳을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the spot where water narrows and flows fast.

phrases.en: The water in the rapids is clear, so you can see the bottom.
phrases.nuance_ko: 여울에서 흐르는 물을 가리켜요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the water flowing in a shallow rapid.

phrases.en: The children carefully crossed the shallow rapids.
phrases.nuance_ko: 얕은 물을 걸어서 지나갈 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A set phrase for wading across shallow water.

explain_en: It is a place in a river where the bed is shallow or narrow, so the current runs fast and makes noise. It suits writing and songs that paint a landscape. A narrowed spot where water rushes is also called '여울목'.

examples.en: I can hear a katydid in the grass.
The child caught a katydid and put it in a container.
Katydids hop around the meadow.

examples.ko: 여름밤에 여치가 울면 시골 생각이 나요.
examples.en: When katydids sing on a summer night, I think of the countryside.

examples.ko: 할아버지가 풀로 여치 집을 만들어 주셨어요.
examples.en: My grandfather made me a katydid house out of grass.
Katydids and bush crickets look alike.

explain: 메뚜기, 베짱이처럼 풀밭에 사는 곤충이에요. 우는 소리는 입이 아니라 날개를 비벼서 내는 소리인데, 한국어로는 그냥 '울다'라고 해요.

phrases.en: Katydids chirp on summer nights.
phrases.nuance_ko: 곤충 소리도 한국어로는 '울다'라고 해요.
phrases.nuance_en: In Korean, insect sounds are also described with 'ulda'.

phrases.en: I fell asleep to the sound of katydids in the countryside.
phrases.nuance_ko: 여름 시골 풍경을 말할 때 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often appears when describing summer countryside scenes.

phrases.example: 풀 위에 여치 한 마리가 앉아 있어요.
phrases.en: A katydid is sitting on the grass.
phrases.nuance_ko: 곤충은 '한 마리'로 세요.
phrases.nuance_en: Insects are counted with 'han mari'.

explain_en: It is an insect of the grass, like the grasshopper and the bush cricket. Its song comes from rubbing its wings, but Korean simply says it '울다' (cries).

en: to be rugged; to be rough; to be jagged

examples.en: The road is bumpy, so it's hard to walk.
I could see bulging muscles on his arm.
My facial skin has become bumpy, and I'm worried.
After the rain stopped, the dirt road is lumpy.
The trunk of an old tree looks knobby.
I fixed the bumpy wall so it's smooth.

explain: 표면이 평평하지 않고 군데군데 불거져 나온 모습이에요. 길, 근육, 피부, 나무껍질처럼 겉이 고르지 않은 것에 써요. 반대로 표면이 고를 때는 '매끈하다'를 써요.

phrases.en: It's hard to ride a bike on a bumpy road.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 앞에서 꾸밀 때 쓰는 모양이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The form used to modify a noun that follows.

phrases.en: This tree bark is rough and bumpy.
phrases.nuance_ko: 문장 끝에서 표면의 상태를 말하는 해요체예요.
phrases.nuance_en: Polite form used to end a sentence describing a surface.

phrases.en: This wall isn't bumpy; it's smooth.
phrases.nuance_ko: 표면이 고르고 매끈할 때 부정형으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Negative form used when a surface is even and smooth.

explain_en: It describes a surface that is not flat and has bumps sticking out here and there. It is used for roads, muscles, skin and tree bark whose surface is uneven. The opposite, for an even surface, is '매끈하다'.

examples.ko: 방 안에 향초 냄새가 은은히 퍼졌어요.
examples.en: The scent of the candle spread softly through the room.
A bell can be heard faintly in the distance.
The moonlight shines gently on the lake.

examples.ko: 그 꽃은 은은히 좋은 향이 나요.
examples.en: That flower has a soft, pleasant fragrance.
Her softly smiling face was really pretty.

examples.ko: 은은히 켜 둔 조명 덕분에 분위기가 좋아요.
examples.en: Thanks to the softly lit lights, the mood is nice.

explain: 소리, 빛, 향기가 뚜렷하지 않고 부드럽게 느껴질 때 써요. 형용사 '은은하다'는 '은은한 향기'처럼 꾸며 주는 말로 쓰고, 좋은 느낌으로 많이 말해요.

phrases.en: The candle softly lit up the room.
phrases.nuance_ko: '은은히'와 거의 같은 뜻이고 일상 대화에서도 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Almost the same as 은은히 and also common in everyday speech.

phrases.en: The flowers give off a faint fragrance.
phrases.nuance_ko: 진하지 않고 부드러운 향기를 좋게 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A positive way to describe a gentle, not-strong scent.

phrases.en: A soft light was on in the alley.
phrases.nuance_ko: 눈부시지 않고 부드러운 빛을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes a light that is gentle rather than dazzling.

explain_en: Gently and faintly, for scents, light, or sounds (창문 너머로 은은히 꽃향기가 날아 들어왔어요.) It is used when a sound, light or scent isn't strong but is felt softly. The adjective '은은하다' is used as in '은은한 향기' (a subtle fragrance), and it usually has a positive feel.

en: to waver; to sway; to shake

examples.en: When the wind blew, the ripples on the lake swayed.
I read a book in a room with a flickering candle.
Longing stirs inside my heart.
The sea, with the water shimmering in the sunlight, was beautiful.
The flame flickered and then soon went out.
The shadows of leaves outside the window sway on the wall.

explain: '흔들리다'는 한 번 크게 움직여도 쓰지만, '일렁이다'는 물결이나 불꽃이 작게 반복해서 출렁이는 모습이에요. '그리움이 일렁이다'처럼 마음이 잔잔히 흔들릴 때도 써요. 활용은 '일렁여요', '일렁였어요'예요.

phrases.en: The candle flame wavers in the wind.
phrases.nuance_ko: '일렁이다'와 거의 같은 뜻이고, 움직임이 반복되는 느낌이 조금 더 강해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Nearly the same as 일렁이다, with a slightly stronger sense of repeated movement.

phrases.en: Looking at the old photo stirred my heart.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물결이나 불빛이 아니라 마음이 잔잔히 흔들릴 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when feelings, not water or light, gently stir.

phrases.en: The sunset light rippling on the sea is really beautiful.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-는' 형태로 뒤의 명사를 꾸밀 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The '-는' form that modifies the noun after it.

explain_en: Near-synonym of 일렁거리다 (일렁거리다); shorter 이다 form, for water or flames swaying gently. '흔들리다' can describe a single big movement, but '일렁이다' describes ripples or flames moving in small, repeated swells. It is also used for a heart gently stirring, as in '그리움이 일렁이다'. It conjugates as '일렁여요' and '일렁였어요'.

examples.en: The ripples moved in gentle waves and sparkled.
The candle flame is flickering and swaying.
Moonlight spreads shimmering over the sea.
I stared for a long time at the flames dancing and flickering.
The shadows wavered on the wall.
Sunlight shines in the water in wavering patterns.

explain: '일렁일렁 흔들리다', '일렁일렁 움직이다'처럼 동사 앞에서 흔들리는 모습을 꾸며요. 물결이나 불빛이 부드럽게 반복해서 움직이는 장면에 잘 어울려요.

phrases.en: The lights reflected in the river sway softly.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가장 기본적인 짝말로, 부드럽게 반복해서 흔들리는 모습을 나타내요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most basic pairing, showing a soft, repeated swaying.

phrases.en: The moon shimmers on the water.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물에 비친 모습이 흔들릴 때 잘 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Fits when a reflection on water wobbles.

phrases.en: The candle flame wavers, so the shadows move too.
phrases.nuance_ko: 불꽃이나 물결이 작게 반복해서 움직이는 모습을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for flames or ripples moving in small, repeated motions.

explain_en: It goes before a verb to describe how something moves, as in '일렁일렁 흔들리다' or '일렁일렁 움직이다'. It suits scenes where ripples or light keep moving softly and repeatedly.

t90.ax: The shadows wavered on the wall.

examples.en: The cherry blossoms are in full bloom in the park.
I took photos while walking along the path of blossoms in full bloom.
The roses are blooming profusely in the yard, so it is full of fragrance.
Butterflies flit among the flowers in full bloom.
The azaleas are in splendid full bloom this year.
At the feast, people had a wild, lively time.

explain: 꽃이 탐스럽게 활짝 핀 모습에 가장 많이 쓰고, 보통 '흐드러지게 피다'로 말해요. 잔치나 놀이가 한창 무르익은 분위기를 말할 때도 '흐드러지게 놀다'처럼 써요.

phrases.example: 흐드러지게 핀 벚꽃 아래에서 도시락을 먹었어요.
phrases.en: We ate lunch boxes under the cherry blossoms in full bloom.
phrases.nuance_ko: '흐드러지다'를 '핀'과 함께 써서 꽃이 탐스럽게 활짝 핀 모습을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Pairs with 'bloomed' to describe flowers blossoming lushly and fully.

phrases.en: I walked along a path of canola flowers in full bloom on Jeju Island.
phrases.nuance_ko: '흐드러진'을 꽃 이름 앞에 붙여 꽃이 가득 핀 풍경을 나타내요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put '흐드러진' before a flower name to show a scene full of blooms.

phrases.en: I had a great time playing with my friends all night.
phrases.nuance_ko: 꽃뿐 아니라 잔치나 놀이가 한창 무르익었을 때도 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Besides flowers, it's used when a party or play is in full swing.

explain_en: Adjective; flowers look lush and overflowing, more poetic than a plain report of bloom (벚꽃이 흐드러지다) It is used most often for flowers blooming lushly and fully, usually as '흐드러지게 피다'. It can also describe a party or play at its liveliest, as in '흐드러지게 놀다'.

t90.ax: At the feast, people had a wild, lively time.

examples.ko: 역사 드라마에는 충신이 간신의 모함에 빠져 귀양을 가는 장면이 자주 나와요.
examples.en: Historical dramas often show a loyal subject framed by a treacherous official and sent into exile.

examples.ko: 왕이 신하를 귀양 보내는 이야기를 읽었어요.
examples.en: I read a story about a king sending a subject into exile.

examples.ko: 귀양에서 풀려난 뒤 그는 고향으로 돌아왔어요.
examples.en: After being released from exile, he returned to his hometown.

examples.ko: 귀양길은 멀고 험해서 많은 사람이 힘들어했대요.
examples.en: They say the road to exile was long and rough, and many people suffered.

examples.ko: 귀양이 끝나자 왕이 다시 그를 불렀어요.
examples.en: When his exile ended, the king called him back.

examples.ko: 귀양지에서 쓴 편지가 지금도 남아 있어요.
examples.en: The letters he wrote in his place of exile still remain today.

explain: 옛날에 죄를 지은 사람을 먼 곳으로 보내 살게 하던 벌이에요. '귀양을 가다', '귀양을 보내다', '귀양에서 풀려나다'처럼 말하고, 주로 사극이나 역사 이야기에서 만나요. '유배'와 같은 뜻으로도 써요.

phrases.example: 그는 십 년 동안 귀양살이를 했어요.
phrases.en: He lived in exile for ten years.
phrases.nuance_ko: 귀양 가서 지내는 생활을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the life lived while in exile.

phrases.example: 그 학자는 왕의 노여움을 사서 유배를 갔어요.
phrases.en: That scholar was sent into exile after angering the king.
phrases.nuance_ko: 귀양과 같은 뜻이고 역사 설명에서 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 귀양; more common in historical explanations.

phrases.en: He was released from exile after three years.
phrases.nuance_ko: 벌이 끝나고 돌아올 수 있게 된다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means the punishment ended and he could return.

explain_en: It was an old punishment in which a person who committed a crime was sent to live in a distant place. It is used as '귀양을 가다', '귀양을 보내다' and '귀양에서 풀려나다', and you mostly meet it in historical dramas and stories. It can also be used in the same sense as '유배'.

t90.ax: When his exile ended, the king called him back.

en: high society; beau monde; social circles

examples.ko: 그녀는 젊은 나이에 사교계의 스타가 됐어요.
examples.en: She became a star of high society at a young age.

examples.ko: 소설 속 주인공이 사교계에 처음 나가는 장면이에요.
examples.en: It's the scene where the novel's heroine first enters high society.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 사교계에서 이름이 알려져 있어요.
examples.en: That person is well known in society circles.

examples.ko: 옛날 유럽의 사교계 이야기를 영화로 봤어요.
examples.en: I watched a movie about old European high society.
I think high society is glamorous only on the surface.

examples.ko: 그는 사교계를 떠나 조용히 살기로 했어요.
examples.en: He decided to leave high society and live quietly.

explain: 상류층 사람들이 모여 어울리는 사회를 말하고, 소설이나 영화, 역사 이야기에서 많이 나와요. 요즘 일상에서는 '인맥이 넓다'처럼 다른 말로 표현해요.

phrases.example: 소설 속 아가씨가 열여덟 살에 사교계에 데뷔해요.
phrases.en: The young lady in the novel makes her debut in high society at eighteen.
phrases.nuance_ko: 소설이나 역사 이야기에서 처음 사교 모임에 나가는 장면에 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often appears in novels and history when someone first enters social gatherings.
phrases.en_equiv: to make a debut in society

phrases.en: That actress was once the belle of high society.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사교계에서 가장 눈에 띄고 인기 있는 여성을 칭찬하는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A compliment for the most noticeable and popular woman in high society.

phrases.en: That lady was famous in high society.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사교계 안에서 이름이 알려진 사람을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for someone well known within high society.
phrases.en_equiv: to be famous in society circles

explain_en: It refers to the world where upper-class people mix and socialize, and it appears often in novels, films and history stories. In daily talk today people use other expressions such as '인맥이 넓다' (to have wide connections).

examples.en: The king stamped the royal seal on the important document.
There was a scene in the drama where they try to steal the royal seal.

examples.ko: 옥새가 없으면 왕의 명령으로 인정받지 못했어요.
examples.en: Without the royal seal, an order was not accepted as the king's command.

examples.ko: 옥새는 박물관 유리 상자 안에 전시되어 있어요.
examples.en: The royal seal is displayed in a glass case in the museum.

examples.ko: 옥새를 지키려고 신하들이 궁궐 문을 닫았어요.
examples.en: The officials closed the palace gates to protect the royal seal.

examples.ko: 문서 아래쪽에 옥새의 붉은 도장이 선명하게 남아 있어요.
examples.en: The red mark of the royal seal remains clearly at the bottom of the document.

explain: 임금이 쓰던 도장을 말해서, 사극이나 역사 이야기에서 들을 수 있어요. 나라를 대표하는 도장은 '국새'라고도 해요.

phrases.en: The king stamped the letter with the royal seal.
phrases.nuance_ko: 옥새를 쓰는 가장 기본적인 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most basic collocation for using the seal.

phrases.en: The king handed the royal seal over to his son.
phrases.nuance_ko: 왕의 자리를 물려준다는 뜻으로 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often means passing the throne on to someone.
phrases.en_equiv: to hand over the royal seal

phrases.en: The national seal is the stamp that represents the country.
phrases.nuance_ko: '옥새'와 비슷하지만 나라를 대표하는 도장을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to 옥새 but refers to the seal that represents the nation.

explain_en: It refers to the seal a king used, so you can hear it in historical dramas and history stories. A seal that represents the nation is also called '국새'.
